issues.desc: Behavioral unit test for fd2_main is DEFERRED to Phase 9 integration (reason proven, not convenience). fd2_main unconditionally issues int386(0x10,...) twice -- INT 10h video mode 0x13 on entry and mode 3 at shutdown -- through the REAL linked Watcom int386. Per the established harness limitation (see 000361cc fd2_dpmi_alloc_dos_memory), the real int386 has no deterministic seam in the DOS/4GW silent harness and a test-local override deterministically crashes/hangs the extender; an INT 10h video mode set in the automated runner is likewise unsafe. fd2_main also (a) calls fd2_main_menu_continue_dispatcher and fd2_load_save_and_init_engine, which live in the SAME translation unit as fd2_main and so cannot be replaced by capture stubs to drive the loop, (b) drives fd2_game_main_loop (the whole-game per-frame dispatcher) whose return value is the inner-loop exit condition, and (c) performs AIL sound init + 8 fd2_load_dat_resource loads + a 152 KB malloc on every entry before the loop is even reached. There is therefore no deterministic unit seam for the outer/inner loop exit logic. The control-flow translation was instead verified statically line-by-line against the disassembly: the EDI(menu_result/exit_outer) and ESI(game_loop_result) state machine (0x25DBD MOV EDI,EAX; chapter-clear arm MOV ESI,1 @0x25DFB; chapter-switch arm MOV EDI,1 @0x25E59 on transition!=0; post-inner CMP ESI,-1/MOV EDI,1 @0x25E7C; menu!=0 arm CMP EAX,-1/XOR EDI,EAX @0x25E88 giving menu_result=0 only when ==-1; outer TEST EDI/JZ 0x25DB1). The RNG warm-up loop bound (int)rand()%0x100 matches MOV EDX,EAX;SAR EDX,31;IDIV 0x100;MOV EDI,EDX (signed remainder) @0x25D90-0x25DAF. The two driver-handle stores match the EAX returns of AIL_install_MDI_INI / AIL_install_DIG_INI; both sample handles take the same DIG driver.

issues.desc: Shared-epilogue equivalence-by-regeneration (pipeline_spec pattern A, rule A-1). fd2_main physically ends with JMP 0x16F04, a tail-jump into the shared epilogue (ADD ESP,0xC; POP EDI; POP ESI; POP EBX; RET) inside fd2_cinematic_scroll_text_up_for_special_scenes @0x16E24 (already emitted, dialog/dialog.c). The merged epilogue is a Watcom code-size optimization; it is NOT reproduced. fd2_main is emitted as a self-contained void function and relies on Watcom 9.5a regenerating an equivalent POP-saved-regs + RET epilogue. Also: __CMain @0x45D4B consumes fd2_main EAX as the DOS exit code (PUSH EAX; JMP _exit @0x36DE4), but the shared epilogue leaves EAX = the last int386 return (BIOS-dependent, a dont-care exit code for a terminating game); the original source is void main(argc,argv) with argc/argv used only by the __CHK frame probe and no explicit return, so void fd2_main(void) is functionally exact. verify_method: post-build -d disasm to confirm the regenerated epilogue + that no caller relies on a specific exit code.

issues.desc: Ghidra decompiled this as __cdecl void with bare 'return;' everywhere, dropping the EAX return values (systematic EAX-tracking bug). The disassembly shows real int returns: most paths XOR EAX,EAX;RET (return 0), but the field-command path @0x118C1-0x118D9 does 'do{r=fd2_field_command_menu_loop();}while(r==0); if(r==1) r^=1; return r;' (MOV EAX,EBX;RET). The single caller fd2_main @0x25DCE consumes EAX (MOV ESI,EAX then TEST ESI;JZ re-invoke), so the return value is load-bearing: a 0 return makes fd2_main loop back into fd2_game_main_loop, non-zero exits. Emitted as int accordingly. Also: the two dispatch-table calls (per_chapter_post_action_handler @0x51B19 and ai_post_action_consequence @0x51B91) push ESI (=selected char idx uVar2) before CALL (PUSH ESI;CALL;ADD ESP,4), so they are invoked with (uVar2); Ghidra rendered them as '()' with no arg — emitted with (sel) per disasm + the (uint32) table prototype in globals.h. Recommend post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical return-value computation and the table-call argument.

AP/DP x1.15 buff. Assembly @0x1B7EF-0x1B819 = FILD/FMUL m64[0x5018D]/CALL __CHP/FISTP. __CHP (0x377A4) sets FPU RC=11 (round-toward-zero) then FRNDINT, so the value is TRUNCATED before FISTP stores it — i.e. assembly truncates, it does NOT round-to-nearest. The emitted C (int)((double)x * 1.15) ALSO truncates toward zero, so the rounding DIRECTION matches. Residual concern is only Watcom 9.5a codegen precision (x87 80-bit FMUL vs C 64-bit double intermediate); for unit-test ground-truth this is bypassed by choosing bases where 80-bit and 64-bit truncation agree (100->114, 200->229, tested in testbtl.c). Still recommend a post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical FILD/FMUL/__CHP/FISTP emission. [reviewer KEEP-confirmed valid] Precision-ordering refinement: the FMUL at 0x1B7F3 runs BEFORE __CHP sets PC=64-bit, so it uses the entry control-word precision. Cross-check: bases 100->114 and 200->229 agree at 64-bit and exact-80-bit truncation; base 40 would give 46 at 64-bit but 45 at exact-80-bit and was correctly AVOIDED in the tests. Unit tests pass under real Watcom, empirically confirming truncation; a post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical FILD/FMUL/__CHP/FISTP emission remains the recommended final check. No code change needed.
issues.reviewer_verdict: KEEP (confirmed valid, no code change needed)

issues.desc: Assembly uses FILD+FMUL+__CHP+FISTP (round-to-nearest by default FPU mode); emitted C uses (int)((double)per_score * multiplier_1_5). For actual values 8*1.5=12 and 24*1.5=36 the result is exact integer so truncation vs rounding doesn't matter, but Watcom codegen may differ.
Assembly 先 REP MOVSD 複製 28-dword resist table 到 stack 再索引；emitted C 直接讀 global。行為等價 (table 不在執行中被修改)，但 machine code 顯著不同。

Equivalence note for the emitter to record: data_fd2_ui_menu_cursor_idx assignment. Asm stores full 32-bit EAX (MOV [0x53c57],EAX at 0x1508b) and then PUSHes that same EAX to fd2_get_item_effect_entry. C truncates to uint8 item_id then zero-extends (uint32)item_id. This is EXACT because the source fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id (0x1b722) ends in MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [EAX]; RET so EAX upper 24 bits are guaranteed 0. The Ghidra decompile CONCAT31(extraout_var,item_id) is conservative-only; the C is correct. Worth a one-line comment in the source so a future reviewer does not re-flag the CONCAT31.

FAITHFUL EQUIVALENCE (not a defect): local 'last_tick' (asm reg ESI) is read-before-write on the first loop iteration -- ESI is never initialized before CMP ESI,EAX at 0x18bc1, and the emitted C 'int last_tick;' is likewise uninitialized, read at input.c:241 before its first assignment at input.c:261. On iteration 1 the status-panel repaint MAY be skipped depending on the garbage value vs the current tick. The emitted C correctly PRESERVES this original (technically-UB) behavior; Watcom 9.5a register-allocates last_tick with no implicit init, matching the original binary. Logged so the intentional non-initialization is documented -- a future tool/reviewer must NOT 'fix' it by zero-initializing last_tick (that would diverge from the binary).

Test deferral for this display-only function is not recorded anywhere (no note in input.c, routing.json, or a tests file). Risk-based policy requires display deferrals be noted with reason. SAME bug just fixed in sibling fd2_execute_attack_damage_calculation @0x1ECC7 (battle.c). The terrain AP/DP block here (battle.c:268-269, 302-316) declares 'uint32 tile_attr_buf;' (4 bytes) + a SEPARATE 'uint8 tile_id;' that is NEVER assigned from the buffer, then indexes data_fd2_battle_tile_attr_mv_modifier_table[tile_id] / _def_modifier_table[tile_id] on the uninitialized tile_id. Out of scope for the 0x1ECC7 fix round (different function); MUST be fixed when fd2_calculate_combat_hit_outcome is reviewed, using the same pattern as the proven-correct btl_ai.c reference (uint8 tile_attr_buf[8]; pass (uint32)tile_attr_buf; tile_id = tile_attr_buf[5]; before each modifier-table index). issues.desc: Equivalence note for emitter record: return-value-in-EAX is a direct memory load (MOV EAX,[0x5275c]) with no intervening CALL, so it is NOT subject to the Ghidra EAX-after-CALL tracking bug; decompiler captured it correctly and no assembly override was needed.

cc justification: __cdecl 1-stack-arg derived from disassembly only (param at [ESP+4], bare RET = caller cleanup), because the function has 0 static callers (cannot derive from caller ADD ESP,K). Preserved-as-original; matches identical sibling @ 0x3615e.

Unit test for the high-risk numeric/branch paths of fd2_dpmi_alloc_dos_memory (CF success/failure branch; the three output computations out_segment=eax<<16 / out_linear=(eax&0xFFFF)<<4 / out_selector=edx&0xFFFF; the off-by-one page-lock arithmetic lock(seg>>12, paragraphs*16+(seg>>12)-1)) is DEFERRED to Phase 9 integration. Reason (proven, not convenience): these paths are reachable only via int386(), which has no deterministic unit-test seam in the DOS/4GW harness. (1) A test-local int386 override to inject the DPMI host result was implemented and proven by bisection to deterministically crash/hang the DOS/4GW runtime -- overriding the CRT int386 breaks the extender's protected-mode interrupt reflection that the CRT itself depends on, so the test executable faults before reaching the dpmi suite; with the override disabled the same build completes (369 pass + the 3 dpmi tests fail on real DPMI non-determinism). int386 is also used by src/input/input.c, whose suite depends on the real INT 16h. (2) Letting the real int386 service INT 31h fn 0x100 allocates real, non-deterministic DOS conventional memory and locks real pages with no paired free here -- leak-prone and unassertable on exact values. Register-liveness edge (-0x11 ENEMY slot1 with target==0x27): the binary animates at the position held in EDI, which can have been set by a *previous* -0x12/-0x14 op (EDI <- current_speaker @0x1628c / runtime_char @0x1642b). This is the documented liveness caveat in the function header. It does not affect compile/exec for the common single-portrait scripts and the first-use/garbage case is equally undefined in both; logged so a future pass can decide whether to mirror EDI exactly across all four portrait branches if such a script sequence is ever observed.

issues.desc: Radial x/y coords use the cos/sin FPU idiom FILD/FMUL/FLD(cos|sin result)/FILD word/FMULP/FADD(P)/__CHP/FISTP at 0x26fa7-0x26ff6 (x) and 0x27005-0x27044 (y). __CHP @0x377A4 sets FPU RC=truncate-toward-zero before FISTP, so the binary TRUNCATES (does not round-to-nearest); emitted C uses (int)(double_expr), which also truncates toward zero, so the rounding DIRECTION matches (same proven pattern as 0x1b750 / 0x15b77). The angle is computed single-precision: binary does FILD dword(i*0x48) / FMUL float[0x3C8EFA2D] / FSTP double, i.e. a float*float product (in x87 80-bit) stored to a 64-bit double then passed to cos/sin; emitted as the identical-shape expression angle_rad = (double)((float)(i*0x48) * pi180.f) with pi180.f bit-cast from the exact 0x3C8EFA2D (value 0.017453277, NOT the textbook pi/180 0.0174532925). Residual concern is ONLY Watcom 9.5a codegen: (a) whether it keeps the float*float product in the 80-bit register before the (double) cast (matching FSTP double) rather than rounding to float first (double-rounding), and (b) x87 80-bit cos/sin/FMUL intermediates vs C 64-bit double. Unit tests bypass this by asserting the libm-INDEPENDENT acc==0 case (cos/sin terms multiplied by 0 -> x=sweep, y=30 exact) plus all integer-only state-4/5 blit-coord arithmetic; the cos/sin-derived non-zero coords are NOT hard-asserted offline. Tests run under the real Watcom 9.5a + its CLIB cos/sin (same routines as the game binary @0x3c885/0x3c898), all PASS. Recommend post-build -d disasm to confirm byte-identical FILD/FMUL float/FSTP double + __CHP/FISTP emission for the angle and both coord stores.

defender_HP_initial ([ESP+0x50]) and defender_HP_after ([ESP+0x58]) are read on paths where the binary leaves them uninitialized (a zero-hit-frame attacker_figani, or scripted mode where the HP-initial load @0x294a9-0x294b1 is skipped). The binary reads stack garbage there. Emitted with an explicit = 0 init to remove the Watcom W202 may-be-uninitialized warning (build is 0-warning). Equivalence: on every path reachable with real FIGANI data (which always has >=1 hit frame), both slots are assigned in the frame loop BEFORE any read, so the init is behavior-identical. In the scripted edge it yields a benign deterministic 0 (the scripted cinematic writes defender.wHP_current = HP_initial - 0; this animation HP is cosmetic, real combat resolution lives elsewhere) instead of UB garbage; no observable game-state difference. verify_method: post-build -d disasm confirms the slots are otherwise untouched on the real-data path.

issues.desc: Behavioral unit test for fd2_chapter_transition_menu is DEFERRED to Phase 9 integration (reason proven, not convenience). The function has two top-level branches and each enters an input-driven do/while loop that only terminates on a real keyboard scancode read through the REAL-linked int386(0x16,...): the STORY branch (category==0) loops until fd2_chapter_transition_with_intro returns nonzero after an INT 16h read, and the BATTLE branch (category!=0) loops on fd2_run_recruitment_or_branch_screen which itself fopens FDICON.B24 and polls the keyboard. Per the established harness limitation (cf. fd2_main @00025bf4 and the display orchestrators), the real int386 has no deterministic seam in the DOS/4GW silent runner and an INT 16h poll cannot be satisfied unattended -> a full-function test would hang. The branch also drives real-linked callees in OTHER translation units that fopen non-staged DAT files where the real loader does exit(1) on failure (the battle save-prompt fd2_display_dialog_scene reads _all_game_text@0x53A7D which the test build does not back with DATO.DAT content; fd2_save_current_state_to_slot fopens FD2.SAV), which would abort the whole run. There is no isolatable pure-logic sub-path: the scancode->cursor radio arithmetic (left 0x4D: --state wrap-to-4; right 0x4B: ++state wrap-at>4 to 0; F8 0x22 debug-bgm cycle %10; metadata-hotkey ptr compare metadata[2]==mode && metadata[1]==state -> state=5; 0xE0/0x52->0x1C Enter remap) is interleaved with fd2_play_sfx_with_handle / fd2_set_bgm_track_with_fade side-effect calls and the active-metadata pointer dereference. The control-flow translation was instead verified statically line-by-line against the disasm: the cdecl 0-param signature + EAX return (1 when story cursor!=2 @0x2CF65 MOV EAX,1; 0 shared @0x2CCFD XOR EAX,EAX for both the battle tail and the story cursor==2 fall-through); the BIOS-tick idle-frame advance uses signed-short delta (3<delta||delta<0) matching MOVSX/SUB/CMP 0x4 JGE / TEST JGE @0x2CDD7-0x2CDE8; the portrait-cache loop stride 80 offset 7 (roster[i].portrait_id) matches SHL2/ADD/SHL4 MOVZX [ECX+EAX+7] @0x2CBC8-0x2CBD2; every CALL-then-EAX use (fopen->fp, typewriter->dialog_result EBX, metadata ptr->BL, load_dat_resource->buffers, recruitment->loop cond, transition_with_intro->commit AL) was checked against assembly for the Ghidra EAX-tracking bug. The intro_panel_idx_lut[category] read reproduces the original 3-byte stack copy of the @0x526D7 table indexed by metadata[0]; the disasm base/index rebasing (intro_const_arr[category-2] with arr[0]=table[2]) is byte-identical to lut[category] over {0x0B,0x3D,0x3E} for the in-range categories 0..2.
